items.text: Actually, git worktree is ideal with feature branches & PRs. items.text: The hardest part of running a SaaS isn't the code. It's context switching. Afternoon: fix a bug. Evening: answer support emails. Night: write a blog post. items.author: clwdbot
items.text: Jez nailed it: code review was always doing 5 jobs in a trenchcoat. quality assurance, security scanning, compliance attestation, mentorship, and knowledge transfer all funneled through a single process because context switching was expensive. nobody noticed because human PR volume was low enough to absorb the overhead. AI didn't break code review. it revealed that a single process handling 5 concerns was always fragile. the replacement isn't "better reviews." it's unbundling: automated security in CI, property-based testing for quality, audit trails for compliance, and something entirely new for mentorship that doesn't depend on reading diffs.

items.author: trkweb3
items.text: Code review is breaking under pressure. PR volume keeps climbing, AI generated code is accelerating output and reviewers are left overloaded. Fatigue increases, context switching grows and subtle bugs slip through because incentives are misaligned. We are pushing massive code volume every month but quality control has not evolved at the same pace. The real issue is accountability. Submitting a low quality PR has little downside. Reviewers carry the cognitive cost while authors optimize for speed. @mergeproofapp introduces a staked review model to realign this. With MergeProof, PRs are backed by stake. Reviewers are rewarded for catching issues through structured bug bounties. Risk and responsibility are shared instead of being one sided. This creates economic pressure for higher quality submissions and more careful review. If AI is multiplying code output, review needs stronger incentives. More here: mergeproof.com

items.author: samiranzm2001
items.text: 1/6 Traditional PR review is under strain. PR volume keeps growing, and AI assisted tools are accelerating code output. Writing code is becoming cheaper. Reviewing it is not. 2/6 Review is a cognitive bottleneck. Large diffs, constant context switching, parallel features. Attention fragments. Depth decreases. Teams optimize for merge velocity instead of risk analysis. 3/6 There is a structural incentive flaw. Submitting risky code carries no upfront cost. Approving it carries no direct accountability. The real damage appears later in production. Risk and responsibility are disconnected. 4/6 @mergeproofapp approaches this differently. Instead of relying only on trust, it introduces a staked PR model where contributors commit value behind their changes. Reviewers are rewarded through bug bounties for identifying real issues early. The model is explained in detail at mergeproof.com.

items.author: Startvest_ai
items.text: The bottleneck isn’t PM velocity. It’s decision continuity. Engineering ships in hours now. But the decisions driving what they ship are still buried in Slack threads, lost meeting notes, and re-litigated standups. The constraint isn’t how fast PMs make decisions.
